entries.proposition: Dosing: XAV939-L1 5 mg/kg intravenously daily for five consecutive days in 6-week-old Shank3b-/- mice; behaviour 24 h after the last dose; the half dose 2.5 mg/kg given as free compound or coated.
entries.snippet: Six-week-old Shank3b-/- mice received daily intravenous injections of XAV939-L1 (5 mg/kg) for five consecutive days, and social behaviors were assessed 24 h after the final injection.

entries.proposition: At 5 mg/kg the prodrug raised AST, ALT, ALP and bile acids and inhibited Wnt in the small intestine; the authors name hepatotoxicity and enterotoxicity.
entries.snippet: These results indicate that, while intravenous XAV939-L1 effectively improves social function, it may induce potential peripheral side effects, such as hepatotoxicity and enterotoxicity.

entries.proposition: At 2.5 mg/kg the uncoated prodrug did not improve social behaviour but still disrupted intestinal villi and raised liver enzymes in wild-type mice: the toxic effect and the beneficial effect are separated by formulation, not by dose.
entries.snippet: In WT mice, H.E. staining showed that XAV939-L1 led to an obvious disruption of the intestinal villi at all segments of the intestine, while XAV939 did not (Figure 6A).

entries.proposition: Brain exposure is read as a fluorescence signal of the Cy5.5 label in excised organs 12 h after 2.5 mg/kg (about 3.4-fold over free label), not as measured drug level; the label rides with the liposome.
entries.snippet: showed approximately a 3.4-times increase in Cy5.5 signal in the brain

entries.proposition: Conversion of the prodrug to XAV939 was shown only in brain homogenate in vitro (about 60 percent loss of prodrug).
entries.snippet: XAV939-L1 decreased by approximately 60% and XAV939 increased dramatically from 1 h of incubation

entries.proposition: The authors reason inhibiting Wnt and glycolysis is "relatively safe" because both are low in mature neurons, citing their own earlier finding that they fall to baseline at 2-3 postnatal weeks; this is a premise about adult brain, not a test in a developing one.
entries.snippet: Inhibiting Wnt signaling and glycolysis for treating ASD is relatively “safe” for brain function, because Wnt/glycolysis levels are low in mature neurons [26,27].

entries.proposition: Unaddressed by the authors: the effectiveness-dosage relationship and effects on human neurons.
entries.snippet: The effectiveness–dosage relationship and the effects of XAV939-L1 on human neurons are also to be investigated.

entries.proposition: The reported brain-targeting route uses allogeneic neuron and astrocyte membranes; the authors list source and chronic immune response as shortcomings.
entries.snippet: The shortcomings of this strategy for clinical application are the source of the neuronal and astrocytic membranes and the chronic immune response if allogeneic neuron–astrocyte membranes were to be repeatedly used.

entries.proposition: Internal inconsistency in the chemistry: Results state L1 was made from XAV939 with acetyl chloride, while Methods synthesise L1 from a phenylurea and a thienopyrimidine and L2 from acetyl chloride; which compound carried the effect is therefore not readable from the text.
entries.snippet: The target product of XAV939-L1 was obtained via reaction of XAV939 with an acetyl chloride under organic base conditions (Figure 1B).

entries.proposition: Behavioural testing was after five daily injections and no outcome beyond 24 h is reported; the Methods do not state blinding or exclusion criteria.
entries.snippet: Mice were trained for three consecutive days before the formal test.
